title: Impact of Metabolic Syndrome and Associated Medication on the Clinical Course, Treatment Requirements, and Complication Rates of Hand Infections – A Retrospective Cohort Study
summary:
This study investigates whether a group of metabolic conditions, known as metabolic syndrome, influences the course of hand infections. These conditions include obesity, high blood pressure, abnormal blood lipids, and elevated blood sugar levels.
The aim is to determine whether patients with these conditions have more severe infections, require more surgeries, or have a higher risk of complications. Additionally, the study evaluates whether medications used to treat these conditions affect the course of infection.
The study is based on existing clinical data. No additional examinations or treatments are performed.
conditions: Arthritis and polyarthritis due to other specified bacterial agents: hand [finger, carpus, metacarpus, joints between these bones]
Disorders of lipoprotein metabolism and other lipidaemias

interventions.name:
Retrospective observational study without intervention. Clinical routine data of adult patients treated for hand infections at the Department of Hand, Plastic, Reconstructive and Burn Surgery, BG Trauma Center Tübingen, between January 1, 2015 and June 30, 2024 will be analyzed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients treated for a hand infection at the Department of Hand, Plastic, Reconstructive and Burn Surgery, BG Trauma Center Tübingen, between January 1, 2015 and June 30, 2024.
Diagnoses including:
paronychia (panaritium)
infectious tenosynovitis
cellulitis (phlegmon)
deep hand infections
septic arthritis (joint empyema)
osteomyelitis of the hand
Age ≥ 18 years
Exclusion criteria:
Incomplete datasets (e.g., missing HbA1c values or missing information on medication).
